sources.title: Core API Reference | Channel
sources.claim_scope: Lower numeric priority is more important; audibility decides within equal priority. Core Channel is not a stereo output channel or an entire Studio event.

sources.title: Core API Reference | ChannelControl
sources.claim_scope: Audibility is an estimate used for resource selection, not an actual waveform measurement.

sources.title: Core API Managing Resources
sources.claim_scope: Finite comparison assumes only the software-channel limit is active. Virtual time, total-capacity stealing, silence thresholds and event-level policies are distinct. Many priority tiers can displace louder lower-priority content.
excluded_claims: No adoption of the unqualified CPU-cost wording
No guarantee of later restoration or audible cue delivery
No generalization of the brief Studio stealing summaries into all Studio policies

sources.title: Core API Reference | System
sources.claim_scope: Software mixed-channel capacity differs from total Channel capacity. No initialization or runtime configuration was executed.

original_example.description: Two active Core channels compete for one real mixing position. Channel capacity retains both. Priorities 64/128 and assumed audibility 0.1/0.8 explain why lowering only the first estimate to 0.05 does not reverse unequal-priority order. Equalizing priorities makes the higher estimate win. Swapping priorities changes resource policy.
assumptions: Total Channel capacity is not exhausted
original_example.status: Original unexecuted reasoning; not measured values or recommended settings
